questions.q: MS Word is a —
questions.solution: Word is the **word processor** of Microsoft Office; Excel is the spreadsheet, PowerPoint the presentation program, Access the database.

questions.q: Which tool **lists all installed hardware along with its drivers** and flags devices that are not working?
questions.solution: **Device Manager** enumerates every hardware component with its driver status — problem devices show a warning mark.

questions.q: The national helpline number for reporting cyber fraud in India is —
questions.solution: **1930** — the national cyber-crime helpline (and cybercrime.gov.in online).

questions.q: Which shortcut captures a **selected part of the screen** with the Snipping overlay?
questions.solution: **Win+Shift+S** opens the snip bar — drag to capture a rectangle, window or full screen.

questions.q: Which of the following situations is most similar to the volunteers' service?
options: A shop raising prices during a festival
A family cooking less food for a small party
A bakery giving its unsold bread at closing time to a children's home
A school collecting fees in advance
questions.solution: The service collects surplus food that would be wasted and gives it to people in need. The bakery does the same thing with unsold bread. Cooking less food reduces waste in a different way (prevention, not redistribution); the other two have nothing to do with surplus food.
questions.shortcut: Write the rule: 'surplus food → people in need'. Only one option follows both halves.
questions.passage:
At a large wedding in the city, caterers often cook for a hundred more guests than are invited, because running short of food is seen as a disgrace to the host family. Much of the extra food is thrown away by midnight.

A group of young volunteers now offers a simple service. Families call a helpline before the wedding, and a van arrives after dinner to collect untouched food, which is taken to night shelters within two hours. The volunteers insist on one rule: they will not accept food that has already been served on plates.

questions.q: Which of the following is most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to **frank** as used in the passage?
questions.solution: Scientists are 'frank about the limits' — they say openly what they cannot do. Frank = honest, open, direct (three synonyms placed as traps). The opposite is evasive — avoiding a clear answer.
questions.shortcut: Three options mean the same thing; the odd one out is the antonym.
questions.passage:
Scientists who study earthquakes are frank about the limits of their craft. They can say which regions are prone to strong tremors and roughly how often such tremors occur, but they cannot yet predict the day or the hour. What they can do is reduce the toll. Buildings that follow earthquake codes sway without collapsing, and a school drill that teaches children to 'drop, cover and hold' can save lives in the first few seconds.

The trouble is that codes cost money and drills take time, while a big earthquake may not come for decades. Officials under pressure to show quick results are tempted to cut corners. When the ground finally shakes, the price of those saved rupees is paid in lives.

questions.q: Parts of a sentence are given as options in order. One part contains an error; the other three are correct. Select the part with the error.
questions.solution: A reported yes/no question takes **whether** (or if) alone: 'wanted to know **whether** I had locked'. 'That whether' stacks two connectives.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To have the upper hand
options: to raise one's hand to ask
to be in a weak position
to have control or an advantage
questions.solution: Upper = above the other. *Have the upper hand* = to be in control or in a stronger position. 'Weak position' is the opposite.

questions.q: The most common **animal motif** on Harappan seals is the —
questions.solution: The **unicorn** (a one-horned bull) appears on the largest number of seals. Other motifs: humped bull, elephant, rhinoceros, tiger.

questions.q: Who is the **chairman** of NITI Aayog?
questions.solution: The **Prime Minister chairs** NITI Aayog. A Vice-Chairperson leads the think-tank work and a CEO (Secretaries-level officer) administers it.

questions.q: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.solution: **Mustard** is sown in October–November and harvested in March–April, so it is a **rabi** crop, like wheat, barley and gram. Paddy, jute and cotton are monsoon-sown **kharif** crops.
questions.shortcut: Winter-sown = rabi; the other three need monsoon water.

questions.q: Sunlight takes about **8 minutes 20 seconds** to reach the Earth. The Earth–Sun distance is nearly —
questions.solution: d = c × t = (3 × 10⁸) × 500 = 1.5 × 10¹¹ m (500 s = 8 min 20 s). This distance is 1 astronomical unit.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $G$ is the centroid and $AD$ is a median. If $AG - GD = 3$ cm, the length of $AD$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $GD = k$; then $AG = 2k$, so $AG - GD = k = 3$.

$AD = AG + GD = 3k = 9$ cm.

questions.q: A road roller of diameter 84 cm and length 120 cm rolls 500 times over a road. The area of the road levelled is: [Use $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution:
The roller levels with its curved surface: $CSA=2\pi rh=2\times\frac{22}{7}\times0.42\times1.2=3.168$ sq m.

Area $=500\times3.168=1584$ sq m.
questions.shortcut: CSA in metres ($r=0.42$ m, $h=1.2$ m) is 3.168, then ×500 = 1584. Trap: 3168 doubles it; 792 halves it.

questions.q: A debt of ₹910 at 20% per annum compound interest is discharged in 3 equal annual instalments. The value of each instalment is:
What is the unit digit of $8^{7^{6}}$?
questions.solution:
Exponent $7^6$: $7 \equiv -1 \pmod 4$ and 6 is even, so $7^6$ leaves remainder 1 with 4.
So $8^{7^6}$ ends like $8^1$ → **8**.

questions.q:
Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd one out.

**Cow, Goat, Buffalo, Tiger**
questions.solution: All four are animals (level one gives no answer). Level two: cow, goat and buffalo are **domestic, plant-eating** animals; the tiger is a **wild, flesh-eating** animal → **Tiger**.

questions.q: Select the related number: **36 : 81 :: 45 : ?**
questions.solution: The digit sum of 36 is 9, and 9² = 81 — **square of the digit sum**. Digit sum of 45 is 9, so 9² = **81**.

questions.q: **P is the husband of Q. R is the father of P.** How is **R related to Q**?
questions.solution: P and Q are married; R is P's father. One marriage crossing from 'father' → R is Q's **father-in-law**.
questions.shortcut: Husband's father = father-in-law; every marriage line adds '-in-law'.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Statue, Status, Station, Statute, Stature.** Which is **third from the left**?
questions.solution: All share STAT. 5th letters: i (Station) vs u (the rest) → Station first. The u-group by 6th letters: e (Statue), r (Stature), s (Status), t (Statute); e < r < s < t. Full order: Station, Statue, Stature, Status, Statute → third = **Stature**.
questions.shortcut: Compare position 6: e < r < s < t — Statue, Stature, Status, Statute.
